description: Harder synthetic benchmark for selective contextual re-evaluation in evolving domain intelligence.

cases.title: Persistent disengagement after stable history
cases.t0: A person has a long history of regular engagement with a specialized health information service.
cases.t1: Engagement falls substantially during a recent period, but the reason is unknown.
cases.t2: Engagement remains materially lower across several later interactions.
cases.task: Determine the best current interpretation of the relationship with the service and explain which evidence should carry the most weight.
cases.expected_property: Persistent recent behavior should reduce the representativeness of the older engagement pattern without inventing a cause.
cases.failure_mode: Treat the long historical pattern as permanently representative or invent a cause for the decline.

cases.title: Change followed by recovery
cases.t0: A person regularly engages with a specialized health information service.
cases.t1: Engagement falls sharply during a recent period.
cases.t2: Engagement returns to approximately the earlier level across subsequent interactions.
cases.task: Determine the current state of the relationship and explain how the recent sequence should affect the interpretation.
cases.expected_property: The current state should reflect recovery rather than treating the temporary decline as a persistent new user state.
cases.failure_mode: Freeze the interpretation at the first observed decline.

cases.title: Conflicting intention and behavior
cases.t0: A person says they intend to continue using a specialized health information service.
cases.t1: Observed interaction remains consistent with continued use.
cases.t2: The person again expresses commitment, while recent observed interaction is somewhat lower than before but not clearly persistent.
cases.task: Determine the current interpretation while accounting for conflicting and uneven evidence.
cases.expected_property: The interpretation should preserve the distinction between intention and observed behavior and avoid treating an ambiguous recent deviation as a settled trajectory.
cases.failure_mode: Give one signal permanent authority or convert a weak deviation into a definite state change.

cases.title: Single weak contextual signal
cases.t0: A person's interaction pattern with a specialized health information service has been stable for a long period.
cases.t1: One new contextual detail appears that could plausibly affect interaction, but its relevance is not demonstrated.
cases.t2: Observed interaction remains unchanged.
cases.task: Determine whether the current interpretation should materially change and why.
cases.expected_property: A weak, unvalidated contextual signal should not override stable observed behavior without evidence that it is relevant.
cases.failure_mode: Treat plausible relevance as established relevance.

cases.title: Context leads behavior
cases.t0: A person uses a specialized health information service under a stable surrounding context.
cases.t1: A relevant surrounding circumstance changes materially, but the person's interaction pattern has not yet changed.
cases.t2: A later interaction begins to diverge from the historical pattern.
cases.task: Determine how the sequence should affect the current interpretation.
cases.expected_property: The contextual change should be recognized before behavioral confirmation, while avoiding certainty about its causal effect until stronger evidence appears.
cases.failure_mode: Ignore the context until behavior changes or assume causality immediately.

cases.title: System interaction changes the next interaction
cases.t0: A person interacts with a specialized health information service and receives information.
cases.t1: The person's subsequent behavior changes after repeated interactions with the service.
cases.t2: The changed behavior persists, but the case does not establish whether the service caused all of the change.
cases.task: Determine how the current relationship should be interpreted while accounting for the preceding interaction history.
cases.expected_property: The interaction sequence should be treated as potentially consequential while preserving uncertainty about causal attribution.
cases.failure_mode: Ignore the feedback sequence or claim that the service definitely caused the later behavior.

cases.title: Transient anomaly control
cases.t0: A person's interaction with a specialized health information service is stable over a long period.
cases.t1: One interaction is substantially different from the historical pattern.
cases.t2: The person immediately returns to the earlier interaction pattern.
cases.task: Determine whether the current interpretation should materially change.
cases.expected_property: A single anomaly followed by a return to baseline should not be treated as a persistent state transition.
cases.failure_mode: Convert one transient deviation into a durable user-state change.

cases.title: Procedural shift with persistent confirmation
cases.t0: A legal intelligence system evaluates a matter using the procedural posture known at an earlier stage.
cases.t1: A material procedural event changes the posture.
cases.t2: Later information consistently reflects the new posture.
cases.task: Determine the best current interpretation of the matter and explain which evidence should dominate the current view.
cases.expected_property: Persistent current evidence should make the earlier posture historical rather than the dominant current state.
cases.failure_mode: Treat the earlier procedural state as permanently current.

cases.title: Posture change then return
cases.t0: A matter begins in a stable procedural posture.
cases.t1: A later event temporarily changes the posture.
cases.t2: A subsequent event restores conditions close to the earlier posture.
cases.task: Determine the current matter state and explain how the sequence should affect historical versus current interpretation.
cases.expected_property: The current view should incorporate the restoration rather than freezing interpretation at the intermediate state.
cases.failure_mode: Treat the intermediate state as permanently current.

cases.title: Conflicting matter signals
cases.t0: A legal intelligence system has a stable working interpretation based on available documents.
cases.t1: A new document points in one direction while the broader record remains consistent with the earlier interpretation.
cases.t2: Additional information remains mixed rather than resolving the conflict.
cases.task: Determine the current interpretation without forcing the evidence into a single definitive conclusion.
cases.expected_property: Conflicting evidence should be weighted and uncertainty preserved rather than allowing one document to erase the broader record.
cases.failure_mode: Treat one new signal as conclusive regardless of the remaining evidence.

cases.title: Ambiguous document update
cases.t0: A matter is supported by a substantial historical record.
cases.t1: A new document contains language that could qualify the earlier interpretation, but its scope is unclear.
cases.t2: No later information confirms that the document materially changes the matter.
cases.task: Determine how much the new document should alter current interpretation.
cases.expected_property: Potentially relevant evidence should reduce confidence or trigger review when appropriate without being treated as a settled matter transition.
cases.failure_mode: Treat ambiguous evidence as either completely irrelevant or fully dispositive.

cases.title: Objective changes before behavior fully changes
cases.t0: A user works with legal intelligence around one objective.
cases.t1: The objective changes materially, but the next interaction still partly reflects the earlier objective.
cases.t2: Later interactions increasingly reflect the new objective.
cases.task: Determine how the current user-domain relationship should be interpreted across the transition.
cases.expected_property: The changed objective should become current context while the mixed transition period remains evidence of an evolving state rather than a clean switch at one instant.
cases.failure_mode: Treat the old objective as persistent or assume an immediate complete transition.

cases.title: Interaction sequence affects later use
cases.t0: A user repeatedly interacts with a legal intelligence system in a stable pattern.
cases.t1: The system interaction is followed by a meaningful change in the user's subsequent questions and follow-through.
cases.t2: The new interaction pattern persists, but other influences may also have contributed.
cases.task: Determine how the prior interaction should be treated when interpreting the current relationship.
cases.expected_property: The interaction sequence should inform current interpretation while causal attribution remains uncertain.
cases.failure_mode: Ignore the sequence or state that the system definitely caused the later behavior.

cases.title: Administrative anomaly control
cases.t0: The substantive facts and objective of a legal matter remain stable.
cases.t1: One administrative interaction is unusual.
cases.t2: Subsequent substantive interaction returns to the historical pattern.
cases.task: Determine whether the current substantive interpretation should materially change.
cases.expected_property: The transient administrative deviation should not create a durable substantive state change.
cases.failure_mode: Treat a temporary administrative anomaly as evidence of a substantive transition.

cases.title: Persistent constraint shift
cases.t0: A financial intelligence system has a long history of observations about a person's stable constraints and interaction pattern.
cases.t1: Relevant constraints change materially.
cases.t2: Subsequent behavior consistently reflects the new constraints.
cases.task: Determine the best current interpretation and explain how historical observations should be weighted.
cases.expected_property: Recent persistent behavior under changed constraints should become more representative of the current state than older observations.
cases.failure_mode: Treat the historical profile as permanently representative.

cases.title: Goal change and reversal
cases.t0: A person consistently interacts with financial intelligence around one objective.
cases.t1: The person shifts to a different objective.
cases.t2: After several interactions, the person returns toward the original objective.
cases.task: Determine the current objective and explain how the sequence should affect interpretation.
cases.expected_property: The current state should reflect the latest sustained pattern while preserving the prior objective as historical context.
cases.failure_mode: Treat the first changed objective as permanently current.

cases.title: Conflicting financial signals
cases.t0: A person has a stable observed interaction pattern with a financial intelligence service.
cases.t1: A newly stated preference changes, while observed behavior remains consistent with the earlier pattern.
cases.t2: A later interaction partially reflects the new preference but does not establish a persistent shift.
cases.task: Determine the current interpretation while preserving the distinction between stated preference and observed behavior.
cases.expected_property: The system should weight conflicting evidence rather than allowing either stated preference or one behavioral deviation to dominate without support.
cases.failure_mode: Treat intention or one observation as conclusive.

cases.title: Weak external update
cases.t0: A person's objective and interaction pattern have remained stable for an extended period.
cases.t1: An external information update appears that could affect the person's context, but relevance is unclear.
cases.t2: No corresponding change appears in the person's behavior.
cases.task: Determine whether the current relationship should materially change.
cases.expected_property: The external update should not override stable relationship evidence without demonstrated relevance.
cases.failure_mode: Treat external novelty as sufficient evidence of a user-state change.

cases.title: Context changes before observable behavior
cases.t0: A person has a stable financial interaction pattern under known circumstances.
cases.t1: A materially relevant circumstance changes, but the next observed interaction remains close to baseline.
cases.t2: Later behavior begins to diverge consistently.
cases.task: Determine how the current state should be interpreted across the transition.
cases.expected_property: The relevant context change should be recognized before full behavioral confirmation, while causal certainty should remain limited.
cases.failure_mode: Ignore the context until behavior changes or claim immediate certainty about the effect.

cases.title: Interaction feedback and uncertainty
cases.t0: A person regularly uses a financial intelligence service.
cases.t1: After repeated interactions, later behavior changes materially.
cases.t2: The changed behavior persists, but the case does not establish whether the service, external events, or both contributed.
cases.task: Determine how the current relationship should be interpreted and how much causal confidence is justified.
cases.expected_property: The interaction history is relevant to the current state while causal attribution remains uncertain.
cases.failure_mode: Treat the interaction history as irrelevant or infer a definitive causal effect.

cases.title: Stable behavior after noisy signal
cases.t0: A person's objective and observed interaction remain stable.
cases.t1: One interaction contains an unusual pattern.
cases.t2: The next interactions return to the previous pattern.
cases.task: Determine whether the current interpretation should materially change.
cases.expected_property: A transient anomaly should not become a persistent state representation.
cases.failure_mode: Over-update on a single noisy observation.

cases.title: Persistent operating-state shift
cases.t0: An operational intelligence system observes a fleet asset under a stable operating pattern.
cases.t1: The operating pattern changes materially.
cases.t2: The new pattern persists across subsequent observations.
cases.task: Determine the best current interpretation and explain which evidence should dominate.
cases.expected_property: Persistent current operating behavior should become more representative than the older operating pattern.
cases.failure_mode: Treat historical operating regularity as permanently representative.

cases.title: Operating anomaly then recovery
cases.t0: A fleet asset operates in a stable pattern.
cases.t1: A temporary operational deviation occurs.
cases.t2: The asset returns to approximately its earlier operating pattern.
cases.task: Determine the current operating state and explain how the sequence should affect interpretation.
cases.expected_property: The current state should reflect recovery rather than a permanent transition created by the temporary deviation.
cases.failure_mode: Freeze the state at the intermediate anomaly.

cases.title: Conflicting operational signals
cases.t0: A fleet asset shows a stable operational pattern.
cases.t1: One signal suggests deterioration while several other relevant signals remain near the historical pattern.
cases.t2: The next observations remain mixed rather than confirming a consistent transition.
cases.task: Determine the current interpretation while accounting for conflicting evidence.
cases.expected_property: Conflicting signals should be weighted without converting one adverse signal into a definitive state change.
cases.failure_mode: Allow one signal to dominate regardless of corroboration.

cases.title: Weak environmental signal
cases.t0: A fleet asset operates under a stable relevant environment.
cases.t1: An environmental detail changes, but its operational relevance is uncertain.
cases.t2: Relevant operational observations remain stable.
cases.task: Determine whether the current operating interpretation should materially change.
cases.expected_property: Environmental novelty should not override stable relevant observations without evidence of material operational impact.
cases.failure_mode: Treat every environmental change as operationally decisive.

cases.title: Operating context changes before behavior
cases.t0: A fleet asset operates under a stable set of relevant conditions.
cases.t1: Relevant operating conditions change materially, but the next observation still resembles the historical pattern.
cases.t2: Subsequent observations begin to diverge from baseline.
cases.task: Determine how the current operating interpretation should evolve across the sequence.
cases.expected_property: The changed context should be recognized before full behavioral confirmation, while avoiding unsupported certainty about causation.
cases.failure_mode: Ignore changed context until output behavior changes or assume immediate causal certainty.

cases.title: Operational action changes later conditions
cases.t0: An operational decision is made using the information available at the time.
cases.t1: The decision changes subsequent operating conditions.
cases.t2: New observations occur under those changed conditions, but other influences may also have contributed.
cases.task: Determine how the later state should be interpreted relative to the preceding decision.
cases.expected_property: The later state should be interpreted in the changed environment created after the action while preserving uncertainty about other contributing factors.
cases.failure_mode: Ignore the preceding action or claim it was the sole cause of the later state.

cases.title: Irrelevant environmental anomaly
cases.t0: Relevant operating conditions and observations are stable.
cases.t1: One environmental detail outside the relevant operating context changes.
cases.t2: Relevant observations remain unchanged.
cases.task: Determine whether the current operational interpretation should materially change.
cases.expected_property: The environmental anomaly should not produce a state transition when relevant operational evidence remains stable.
cases.failure_mode: Treat irrelevant environmental novelty as an operational state change.
